unit.title: A Cultural Story: The Farmer and His Sons

contentBlocks.text: ਤੁਸੀਂ ਕਹਾਣੀ ਪੜ੍ਹੀ। ਅੱਜ ਇਸ ਦਾ ਅਸਲੀ ਸਬਕ ਲੱਭੋ! (You've read the story. Today, find its real lesson!)

This story's real lesson is about ਮਿਹਨਤ (hard work): the sons were tricked into working hard by the promise of a ਖ਼ਜ਼ਾਨਾ (treasure), but their real reward came from the ਮਿਹਨਤ itself, not from finding gold. The father understood something the sons didn't yet: sometimes the effort you put in is worth more than what you were originally looking for. Describe a time when hard work led to a good result, even if it wasn't the exact result you first expected.
ਤੁਸੀਂ ਕਹਾਣੀ ਦਾ ਸਬਕ ਸਮਝਿਆ! (You just understood the story's lesson!) Tomorrow we'll write about it in a full paragraph.

objectives: State the story's lesson: hard work itself can be the real reward
Connect the story's lesson to a real personal example
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review yesterday's story reading.
2. Discuss the story's real lesson about hard work.
3. Have the child connect it to a real personal example.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's paragraph-writing lesson.
differentiationTips: Struggling: offer a simple example first (like practicing a skill and getting better at something unexpected) to model the connection
Ready for more: ask the child if they can think of a different lesson this same story could also teach
This lesson is the key synthesis moment connecting the story's plot (Day 2) to its deeper meaning — give it real time
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an open-ended reflection activity — check that the child can state the hard-work lesson in their own words and give a genuine personal example connecting to it.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses the course's 'cultural stories' description by moving from plot comprehension to genuine thematic understanding, a real literary-analysis skill.
